sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Rejection of Compulsion**: The government explicitly refused to accept the principle of **compulsory primary education**, citing administrative and financial constraints.
• **Shift to Quality**: The policy prioritized the **improvement of existing schools** over the rapid expansion of new, low-quality primary schools.
• **University Expansion**: It advocated for the establishment of **teaching and residential universities** in every province to move away from the purely affiliating model.
• **Private Enterprise**: Continued reliance on **grant-in-aid** to private institutions while maintaining strict government supervision.

Financial assistance provided by the colonial state to private schools, contingent upon meeting government-set quality standards.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Teacher Training**: Increased funding for training colleges to improve pedagogical standards.
• **Curriculum Reform**: Emphasis on practical subjects and vernacular instruction at the primary level.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Chronic underfunding and the elitist nature of the policy.
• **Solutions**: The policy paved the way for the Sadler Commission (1917) to address the structural flaws in university education.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'Q-R-U' (Quality, Rejection, Universities).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Quality over quantity in primary, Rejection of compulsion, Universities (residential) focus.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 1913 Resolution with the 1911 Gokhale Bill. Remember: 1911 was the *demand* for compulsory education; 1913 was the *official government rejection* of that demand.
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'Elitist bias in colonial education' when discussing the 1913 Resolution's failure to promote mass literacy.

keyTakeaways: The 1913 Resolution formally abandoned the goal of universal primary education.
It shifted the focus from the 'affiliating' university model to the 'teaching and residential' model.
It reinforced the role of the state as a supervisor of private educational initiatives.
